details.label: Summary
details.text: Scattered thunderstorms will develop eastward into the Black Hills/western South Dakota vicinity through this afternoon, bringing a threat for large to very large hail and severe wind gusts

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest radar imagery depicts a developing supercell in close proximity to a surface low across northeastern Wyoming. Aided by weak ascent ahead of a mid-level perturbation and easterly, upslope flow (surface dewpoints ranging from the low 60s F to near 70 farther east), convection will expand in coverage through the afternoon as it evolves eastward into the Black Hills/western South Dakota vicinity. While the 18z UNR observed sounding depicted lingering inhibition, filtered diurnal heating should gradually reduce inhibition through the afternoon. For ongoing/developing convection, steep mid-level lapse rates (8+ C/km), 40-50+ kts of effective shear, and relatively straight, elongated hodographs will support supercells as the initial storm mode, with large to very large hail the primary hazard. Increasing storm coverage lends uncertainty to how long discrete supercells will be maintained, with eventual upscale growth/cluster development expected to yield a transition towards severe wind gusts as the primary hazard. Should a discrete mode be maintained for longer, however, very large hail to 3 inches in diameter would be possible. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed for a portion of the area within the hour

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Recent trends in volumetric radar data indicate deeper convective updrafts forming on the western flank of the MCS, near Terre Haute. That area coincides with where the MCS intersects a residual outflow boundary that extends south-southeast into south-central KY. Low-level convergence/ascent along that boundary in conjunction with the influx of a moderately to strongly unstable air mass from the west is expected to support further storm intensification this afternoon over portions of central and southern IN. Damaging winds with localized gusts up to 75 mph will be the primary hazard. Some brief tornado potential may materialize to the immediate east of the outflow boundary, where locally backed near-surface winds enhance low-level shear. The severe threat is expected to spread south of the current watch area in far southern IN into central KY, where a new watch will likely be required

details.label: Summary
details.text: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms will pose an isolated risk for large hail and damaging wind gusts this afternoon from the Niagra Frontier into the Northern Tier of PA

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms are ongoing across southern Ontario and portions of the Niagra Frontier as of 1710 UTC, with this activity forecast to develop southeastward into southern NY/northern PA through this afternoon. While surface temperatures remain seasonably cool in the low-to-mid 70s F, surface dewpoints in the low-to-mid 60s F and regionally steep mid-level lapse rates of 6-7 C/km are supporting modest buoyancy, with 1000 to locally 1500 J/kg MLCAPE indicated by recent objective analysis. Concurrently, a mid/upper-level speed max will continue to shift eastward from Lower Michigan into NY/PA through this afternoon and evening. This enhanced mid/upper flow (sampled by the BUF VAD profile and the 12 UTC BUF observed sounding) will continue to promote effective shear of 30-40 kts and elongated hodographs favorable for supercell structures. The primary risks associated with this activity will be large hail and damaging wind gusts. Current expectations are for convective coverage and the severe risk to remain too isolated for watch issuance; however, a targeted Severe Thunderstorm Watch could be considered should greater storm/severe coverage prevail

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Forcing for ascent within the southwest flank of an MCV moving through the lower Savannah River Valley will combine with broadly confluent low-level flow to yield scattered thunderstorms this afternoon. Area VWPs indicate relatively weak vertical shear across the region, which will limit the potential for storm organization. However, the 12Z JAX sounding sampled the presence of a very moist and strongly unstable air mass with MLCAPE of 3000-3500 J/kg. As such, the potential will exist for locally intense wet microbursts capable of a few damaging wind gusts, especially if storms can merge into clusters
